WSL3 is the app version. The underlying mechanism of how Windows runs Linux hasn't changed. The change from WSL to WSL2 was in that mechanism (WSL: run via syscall translation, WSL2: run via VM). This is an app change, so it covers the interfaces of how you can start running Linux code, but underneath the hood, it's still a kernel running within a VM.

The big addition here is the support for containers. The app now provides a simple way to run containers directly. Underneath the hood, there's still a kernel running on a VM, though. There's also some improvements to the filesystem layer, a kernel upgrade, etc.

I think this is fair the majority of time, but I'd like to mention Zig, since Zig has a convention of all allocations being fallible and handled. It's a pain at first to handle error.OutOfMemory at each allocating site, but I feel like I'm much more conscious of where allocation can fail and how to gracefully handle it. I've also gotten a lot better at transactions since pretty much every operation has failure points now.

In fact I've written a whole interpreter that can recover from OOM by raising a recoverable exception to the user. It's really only because Zig made recovering idiomatic, and I'm not sure I could've done it in another language (maybe Rust but I'd have to rewrite large parts of stdlib to both return an error and take a custom allocator).
